spec.goal: Add an optional `?offset=N` query parameter to `GET /items` in `toy/src/app.js`. `N` must be a canonical non-negative decimal integer (`/^(0|[1-9][0-9]*)$/`, within `Number.isSafeInteger` range); any other present value returns `400 {"error":"invalid offset"}`. The offset skips the first `N` results of the existing pipeline after the sort stage and before the `?limit` cap, making the full pipeline `filter (?q) -> sort (?sort) -> skip (?offset) -> cap (?limit)`. An absent `offset` and `offset=0` are both no-ops; an offset at or beyond the number of available results returns `200 []`. Query-parameter validation order is pinned as q -> sort -> offset -> limit so a request with several invalid parameters yields one deterministic error body. All existing routes, error shapes and the `Item` shape are unchanged, and the whole existing suite still passes — including `toy/test/integration-r5.test.js`, whose "unknown params are ignored" case at line 125 uses `offset=1` as a *sample unknown parameter* and must be updated to the new semantics.

acceptance.given: an app with items named a, b, c created in that order
acceptance.when: GET /items is requested with no offset parameter
acceptance.then: the response is 200 with [a, b, c] — byte-identical to the pre-change behavior for every existing q/sort/limit combination

acceptance.given: an app with items a, b, c
acceptance.then: the response is 200 with [a, b, c], identical to the response for GET /items with offset absent

acceptance.given: an app with items a, b, c
acceptance.then: the responses are 200 [b, c] and 200 [c] respectively, preserving insertion order and full Item objects (id, name, tags, created_at)
each response is 200 with an empty array [] and content-type application/json — never a 400 and never a 404

acceptance.given: items created in insertion order banana, apple, cherry, mango
acceptance.then: the response is 200 with the names [banana, cherry] — proving the skip runs after the sort stage and before the limit cap (a skip-before-sort implementation would yield [apple, cherry]; a cap-before-skip implementation would yield [banana])

acceptance.given: items named alpha, beta, alphabet, gamma in that insertion order
acceptance.then: the response is 200 with only [alphabet] — the q filter runs first against the full list, so the skip counts only items that survived the filter

acceptance.given: an app with at least one item
acceptance.when: GET /items?offset=X is requested for each X in -1, -0, 1.5, 1e1, 0x1, 01, 00, abc, true, '' (bare ?offset= and ?offset with no '='), '%201' and '1%20'
acceptance.then: every response is 400 with content-type application/json and body exactly {"error":"invalid offset"}

acceptance.given: an app with at least one item
acceptance.when: GET /items?offset=1&offset=2 (Express parses this as an array) and GET /items?offset[x]=1 (parsed as an object) are requested
acceptance.then: both return 400 with body {"error":"invalid offset"} — a non-string offset is never coerced

acceptance.given: an app with at least one item
acceptance.then: the response is 400 with body {"error":"invalid offset"}, matching the existing limit boundary rule

acceptance.given: an app with at least one item and validation order pinned as q -> sort -> offset -> limit
acceptance.when: GET /items?sort=bogus&offset=-1&limit=0, GET /items?sort=name&offset=-1&limit=0 and GET /items?sort=name&offset=1&limit=0 are requested
acceptance.then: the bodies are exactly {"error":"invalid sort"}, {"error":"invalid offset"} and {"error":"invalid limit"} respectively — one deterministic 400 per request, never a 500, never a partial list, and the two pre-existing combined-error cases (?sort=bogus&limit=0 -> invalid sort, ?sort=name&limit=0 -> invalid limit) keep their current bodies

acceptance.when: a request with an invalid offset is rejected and then GET /items and POST /items {name:'d'} are issued
acceptance.then: GET /items still returns the same 3 items in the same order and the new item receives id 4 — a rejected request mutates no stored state and consumes no id

acceptance.given: an app with one item of id 1
acceptance.then: the responses are 200 with the item and 404 {"error":"not found"} — offset is ignored and never validated outside the GET /items collection route, exactly as limit is today

acceptance.given: the request logger enabled with NODE_ENV != 'test'
acceptance.then: the logged line is 'GET /items 200 <ms>' with no query string, and the response body is unaffected — the logger, the JSON 404 catch-all, GET /health, POST /items and DELETE /items/:id are all unchanged

acceptance.given: toy/test/integration-r5.test.js line 125 currently asserts GET /items?limit=1&offset=1&foo=bar returns [a], using offset as a stand-in for an ignored unknown parameter
acceptance.when: that assertion is updated to the new semantics (offset=1 then limit=1 over [a,b,c] yields [b]) while keeping a genuinely unknown parameter such as foo=bar in the case
acceptance.then: `cd toy && npm test` reports 35/35 existing tests passing plus every new offset test passing, 0 failures

acceptance.given: toy/README.md documents the filter -> sort -> cap pipeline and the ?sort and ?limit parameters
acceptance.then: the README describes the pipeline as filter -> sort -> skip -> cap, documents ?offset=N (canonical non-negative integer, 0 allowed, past-the-end returns [], invalid returns 400 {"error":"invalid offset"}), and the doc comment above the GET /items handler in toy/src/app.js states the same contract including the q -> sort -> offset -> limit validation order

touched_surfaces.ref: toy/src/app.js -> createApp() -> app.get('/items') handler: validation block and pipeline stages

out_of_scope: GET /items/:id, POST /items, DELETE /items/:id, GET /health and the JSON 404 catch-all — no behavior change beyond ignoring an offset query parameter as they ignore limit today
The Item shape { id, name, tags, created_at } — no new fields, no pagination metadata on items
Pagination envelopes: no total/count field, no X-Total-Count or Link/next headers, no { data, meta } wrapper; GET /items keeps returning a bare JSON array
Cursor- or keyset-based pagination, page/per_page aliases, or any parameter other than offset
Changing the semantics, validation regexes or error strings of ?q, ?sort or ?limit; ?limit keeps rejecting 0 while ?offset accepts 0
Changing the persistence layer — the in-memory Map, insertion ordering and per-app-instance isolation stay as they are
The request logger format (wi-9), including whether query parameters appear in the logged path
toy/package.json: no version bump, no new dependencies, no change to the test script
toy/src/server.js, ports and hosting config (brief.json hosting.envs), CI, and anything under substrate/ or .claude/
Performance work: slice-based skipping over the existing array copy is sufficient; no indexing or lazy iteration
risk_reasons: Purely additive optional query parameter—clients not sending offset see identical behavior (AC-1 byte-identical requirement)
No breaking changes to existing client contracts—offset absence and offset=0 both no-ops (AC-12 confirms offset ignored outside /items collection route)
Stored data shape unchanged—affects only retrieval pipeline order, not Item shape {id, name, tags, created_at} or persistence layer
No auth, secrets, payments, or infrastructure impact—purely a stateless filtering parameter on in-memory collection
Fully reversible—parameter can be deprecated without breaking existing clients
All 35 existing tests required to pass (AC-14), with only test semantics updated for the new parameter, not test structure
Deterministic error handling—invalid offset returns existing 400 error shape, validation order defined without interfering with existing parameters

tasks.description: Implement ?offset=N query parameter for GET /items with validation (canonical non-negative integers, safe integer range), pipeline integration (after sort, before limit), validation order (q → sort → offset → limit), update integration test line 125, and document the new parameter
